concerns: Assay sensitivity and validation: BODIPY C11, TBARS and permeability-dye assays can be insensitive or interfered-with at the low particle/protein mass typical of capture-positive eluates; the proposal rightly calls out LLOQ and spike-in controls but these must be demonstrated before decision-making. (ev-misev2023-quality-framework)

Specificity for EV membranes: Peroxidation or dye signals may arise from non-vesicular lipid particles, lipoproteins, or free oxidized lipids co-isolated with EVs; targeted oxidized-phospholipid LC-MS and orthogonal fractionation/density controls are required to attribute signal to EV membranes. (ev-misev2023-quality-framework)

Interference from buffers/excipients and capture-elution reagents: Fluorescent reporters and TBARS chemistry are prone to interference by formulation components or elution buffers; stringent buffer-compatibility and spike-recovery controls are essential to avoid false positives/negatives. (ev-misev2023-quality-framework)

Discrimination vs epitope masking: Loss of capture-based signals may reflect conformational epitope masking or surface-protein alteration without chemical membrane damage; the experiment must include controls (e.g., detergent/protease treatments, proteomic checks) that can partition epitope-related loss from lipid-chemistry-driven loss. (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi)

Predictive value for in vivo delivery: Non-human-primate data show intranasal EVs can be retained in the nasal cavity and show negligible brain uptake regardless of in vitro signatures; chemistry flags may be necessary but not sufficient predictors of in vivo exposure/failure—bridging in vivo recovery experiments stratified by chemistry status are needed before gating potency studies. (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution)

Material requirements and reproducibility: Low-biomass capture-positive fractions limit capacity for confirmatory LC-MS and replication; ensure >=3 independent lots and plan material allocation/prioritization. (ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi)

Potential for false reassurance or over-reliance: A negative chemistry flag (no peroxidation/permeability change) does not ensure in vivo delivery or potency, given species/delivery route challenges and other failure modes (clearance, uptake), so these attributes should gate but not replace downstream in vivo or orthogonal potency linkage studies. (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution)
conclusion: The proposed chemistry-centered stability attributes (BODIPY C11/TBARS peroxidation and membrane-permeability dye uptake on capture-positive particle fractions) are a plausible and useful orthogonal approach to detect physicochemical membrane damage that could precede loss of capture-protection signatures. The approach is consistent with MISEV recommendations to use orthogonal characterization and with rodent studies showing intranasal EV sensitivity to processing, but there is moderate uncertainty about assay sensitivity on low-biomass fractions, specificity for bona fide EV membranes (vs co-isolated lipid complexes), and predictive value for in vivo delivery in larger species. The experiment as designed can discriminate some competing explanations (chemical membrane damage versus preserved membranes with epitope masking) provided the necessary controls (detergent positive control, spike-in recovery, buffer-compatibility checks, and LC-MS confirmation) are included and assay performance is established. However, further bridging experiments (including short-interval in vivo recovery or NHP-relevant assays) will be required to demonstrate that these chemistry flags predict loss of in vivo detectability or function.
evidence_gap: Key gaps: (1) direct, within-lot correlation data linking measured lipid peroxidation/permeability changes to concurrent loss of capture-protection and protected-cargo signals across controlled failure exposures; (2) demonstration of assay sensitivity, linearity, and LLOQ on capture-eluted, low-biomass fractions; (3) evidence that measured chemistry changes originate from EV membranes rather than co-isolated soluble lipid-containing complexes (requiring orthogonal LC-MS and/or density/fractionation controls); (4) predictive validation that chemistry-centered flags map to reduced in vivo recoverability or function in a larger-animal or clinically relevant delivery context.
